summary: Cupid makes condoms, water-based lubricants and diagnostic test kits. It supplies organisations that buy in bulk and also sells products such as deodorants through shops and distributors.
description: Cupid makes and packs items for two kinds of customer. A public health organisation may order a large batch of condoms to distribute. A shop can buy Cupid-branded fragrance or personal care products through a distributor, then sell a pack at a time to shoppers.
money: Cupid earns from shipping and selling finished goods. Its costs include materials, packaging, factory staff, running equipment and sending orders. Selling consumer products also takes promotion and a network to stock shops. A bulk order may be recorded as a sale before the buyer pays.
customers: Health agencies, governments, distributors and other business buyers place bulk orders. In consumer retail, distributors and stores buy products for resale, while shoppers buy the final packs.
drivers: How often big buyers place orders, how quickly stores reorder consumer products and how much Cupid spends making and selling each pack.

quick.title: What does it do?
quick.text: It makes condoms, lubricants and test kits and sells consumer products such as deodorant.

quick.title: Who pays?
quick.text: Health programmes and distributors may buy in bulk. Shops stock packs for individual shoppers.

quick.title: How does it earn?
quick.text: It earns when it sells finished products and meets the terms of delivery.

quick.title: What does it spend on?
quick.text: Materials, packaging, staff, factories and getting products into shops and to larger customers.

groups.title: Bulk condom orders
groups.explanation: Organisations can buy and distribute finished packs under public health programmes.

groups.title: Lubricants
groups.examples: Water-based lubricant jelly in packaged formats.
groups.explanation: Cupid sells the gel through its product distribution routes.

groups.title: Tests done outside the body
groups.examples: Rapid diagnostic kits and pregnancy test kits.
groups.explanation: The kits are sold to buyers that need a packaged test for a sample.

groups.title: Personal care products
groups.examples: Cupid and Cupid Angel deodorants, perfumes and other consumer products.
groups.explanation: The company reaches shoppers through stores and consumer distribution.

basics.title: What is a tender?
basics.text: A tender is a buyer’s invitation for competing suppliers to offer prices, delivery schedules and other terms. The size of an order can change from one award to the next.

basics.title: What is a distributor?
basics.text: A distributor buys or moves stock from a maker to many shops. Supplying a distributor can reach shoppers far beyond the factory.

stepsTitle: From materials to a paid order

steps.title: Receive a buyer’s order
steps.text: A large buyer chooses quantities and terms or a distributor orders packs for stores.

steps.title: Make, test and pack goods
steps.text: The factory prepares the goods and checks the batch before it leaves.

steps.title: Ship and record the sale
steps.text: The goods go to the buyer or distributor. The payment date depends on the agreed terms.

steps.title: Collect payment
steps.text: Cash arrives when the buyer settles the bill. The sale must cover the cost of manufacturing, shipping and promoting the goods.

specifics.title: Bulk buying can arrive in bursts
specifics.text: A public tender can supply many packs at once. A repeat shop order typically serves a smaller purchase, and may come more often.

specifics.title: Qualification is part of selling
specifics.text: Some institutional buyers require a manufacturer to pass product and factory approval checks before it can bid.

specifics.title: Retail adds a different expense
specifics.text: Getting fragrance onto shelves requires distribution and promotion. The buyer’s first order is useful only if shoppers keep buying.

watch: A first shipment to new stores only tells you the shop took stock.
Read Cupid’s presentation for consumer sales and any evidence of reorders or stock the shops sold.
Do big orders move from announcement to delivery?
An award can bring sales across multiple periods.
Compare order announcements with finished shipments and reported sales. Check if the announced order sets a delivery timetable.
What share comes from each product family?
Condoms and personal care can involve different manufacturing and selling costs.
Check the company’s sales mix, then look for what the financial statements disclose about profits.
Is cash coming in as sales grow?
Customers can owe more money when bulk orders rise.
Compare the unpaid customer bills and cash from operations with revenue. Look for the share of bills past their payment dates.
How much profit comes from making and selling goods?
An investment revaluation also affects reported profit.
Read the audited expense and other income rows separately from product sales. Check whether the change in investment value required a sale.
risks: A change in health budgets or tender schedules can move bulk orders to another period.
A product fails a buyer’s checks
A rejected batch can delay shipment and add replacement or testing costs.
The value in rupees can change when overseas buyers pay in another currency.
Shops have limited shelf room and may give it to better-selling products.

helps.title: One factory network makes related goods
helps.text: Related packaged products can be sold to buyers that already need procurement and delivery.

helps.title: Different buyers place different orders
helps.text: Institutions can take large shipments while retail stores can serve people buying one pack.

helps.title: Product approvals open some bulk orders
helps.text: Meeting a programme’s requirements makes Cupid eligible for some orders with strict purchase rules.

hurts.title: Retail ranges need promotion
hurts.text: A retail buyer can choose another brand even if the store stocks Cupid.

hurts.title: Expansion spends money before orders arrive
hurts.text: Equipment and facilities have to be paid for before they make enough products to cover their cost.

hurts.title: Large buyers may take time to pay
hurts.text: Outstanding bills can use up cash that would otherwise fund the next batch.

context: November 2026: Cupid publishes a breakdown of its sales by product
The latest investor presentation separates sales of male and female condoms, test kits and consumer products. It also distinguishes these sales from other operating revenue.

financialNotes.title: Read product sales separately from other gains
financialNotes.text: The table covers Cupid and the companies it controls. Annual profit includes changes in what investments were worth on paper, which are different from cash received from customers.

financialNotes.title: Use the sales mix for what sold
financialNotes.text: Cupid discloses product sales in its presentation. The table does not assign annual profit to each product.

financialCue: Read operating revenue alongside group profit, and check the change in investment values shown in the accounts.
